headline: A 22-year-old Tesla driver in California told investigators he was asleep with Full Self-Driving switched on when his car drove into a closed freeway lane and hit a highway patrol car, seriously injuring two officers.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered by 1: the crash was on 13 Oct 2026 and first reported 14 Oct 2026; today's news is the released video and the driver's statement, and the claim that the system was on is unverified.
importance_line: Drivers and road workers are at risk when people treat Tesla's supervised driving system as a self-driving car, and regulators may look again at it, but so far the claim that it was engaged comes only from the driver.
summary: CBS News Sacramento reports that the California Highway Patrol released dashcam video of a Tesla hitting a patrol car at freeway speed on Interstate 80 near Fairfield late on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026, seriously injuring two officers who are now recovering. The patrol says the 22-year-old driver told investigators he had been asleep with Full Self-Driving on, and it stressed that the system is driver assistance that requires the driver to stay alert and in control.
notes: Read at CBS News Sacramento because the ABC News pool link is a video page. Crash 13 Oct 2026; new today: CHP video and the driver's statement. The Full Self-Driving claim is the driver's account; Tesla's own comment was not in the text read. A vehicle in assisted-driving mode drove into the closure (supervised system, not a driverless car).
